smell: PrefixMap validates keys with PrefixMapSchema = S.Record(S.String, IRI).check(PrefixMapKeyChecks) and then uses a repo-banned double cast to recover S.Codec<Readonly<Record<PrefixLabel, IRI>>, ...>. The schema key proof is outside the Record key schema, so TypeScript cannot carry the branded PrefixLabel key type without `as unknown as`.
proposedTarget: Use the branded key schema directly: S.Record(PrefixLabel, IRI), then annotate it as PrefixMap. Effect v4 Record accepts a key schema (verified at .repos/effect-v4/packages/effect/src/Schema.ts:3780-3793), and its decoded Record.Type indexes by Key["Type"] (verified at .repos/effect-v4/packages/effect/src/Schema.ts:3643-3648), so PrefixLabel checks move into the key codec and the cast plus PrefixMapKeyChecks/isPrefixLabel helper can disappear.

smell: ProvRecord is a 19-member S.Union where the entity/agent classes carry provType tags (for example Entity at lines 262-265 and Agent at lines 349-352) but the relation classes Usage through End have no discriminator fields (for example Usage at 593-598 and Generation at 623-628). The public union therefore cannot derive ProvRecord.match/.guards via S.toTaggedUnion, and docs still show S.is(Agent) branch narrowing at lines 912-915.
proposedTarget: Add provType: S.tag("Usage" | "Generation" | ... | "End") to the relation classes, then pipe ProvRecord through S.toTaggedUnion("provType"). In-repo exemplars: Rdf.ts:536-537 derives Term with S.toTaggedUnion("termType"), Evidence.ts:194-195 derives EvidenceSelector with S.toTaggedUnion("kind"), and WebAnnotation.ts:161-166 derives WebAnnotationSelector with S.toTaggedUnion("type"). This is a public wire-form change and needs the SPEC §5.4 consumer sweep plus encoded snapshot proof.

smell: webAnnotationSelectorToEvidenceSelector manually dispatches a schema-tagged WebAnnotationSelector with Match.value(selector), two Match.when({ type: ... }) arms, and a Match.orElse fallback that silently treats every future selector type as FragmentSelector. WebAnnotationSelector already derives .match from S.toTaggedUnion("type") at lines 161-166.
proposedTarget: Replace the Match.value pipeline with WebAnnotationSelector.match(selector, { TextQuoteSelector: ..., TextPositionSelector: ..., FragmentSelector: ... }). Same-file exemplar: evidenceSelectorToWebAnnotationSelector already uses EvidenceSelector.match at lines 275-296; another package-local exemplar is Term.match in Rdf.ts:1106-1115.

smell: ProvO = S.Union([ProvBundle, ProvRecord]) is a public entrypoint union that a broad undiscriminated-union detector can flag as another S.toTaggedUnion candidate.
proposedTarget: None -- keep as-is after the ProvRecord discriminator gap above is handled.

exception.reason: ProvO deliberately accepts either a bundle object ({ records, lifecycle? }) or a single PROV record as the public convenience entrypoint. Adding a wrapper discriminator to ProvBundle would change the documented simple bundle payload shape; the actionable exhaustiveness gap is inside ProvRecord, where relation records lack their own provType tags.

smell: JsonLdContext.terms uses S.Record(S.String, S.Union([S.String, JsonLdTermDefinition])), which a broad undiscriminated-union detector can mistake for a tagged-union candidate.

exception.reason: JSON-LD 1.1 term definitions are externally specified as either a compact IRI string or an expanded term-definition object. Adding a discriminator would stop accepting the standard JSON-LD context wire form; the two shapes are structurally disjoint (string vs object) and decode unambiguously at the boundary.

smell: JsonLdPropertyValue = S.Union([JsonLdReferenceValue, JsonLdLiteralValue]) is an undiscriminated object union over JSON-LD @id-reference and @value-literal forms, and examples narrow with S.is(JsonLdLiteralValue) at lines 341-345.

exception.reason: The discriminator is the JSON-LD standard shape itself: node references carry @id, value objects carry @value. Injecting a first-party tag would change the accepted/encoded JSON-LD wire object, and the required keys make the branches structurally disjoint.
